html:
SMTO-MEM-0003 — This memory's key isn't allowed

GUID: 5b5d91b4-9ded-4a6c-8fd7-6fd9f871de70
Slug: memory-invalid-key
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: mem

What happened

  • SMTO didn't save this memory because its key (the short name that identifies it) uses characters or a length SMTO doesn't accept. Nothing was saved or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Memory Editor, change the new memory's Key so it uses only letters, numbers, periods (.), underscores (_), colons (:) and hyphens (-). Remove spaces, slashes and accented letters. SMTO accepts only these plain characters in a key, so any other character causes this rejection. A saved memory's key can't be renamed later, so it's worth getting right now.
  2. Make sure the key isn't empty and is no longer than 160 characters, then select Save. An empty key or one over 160 characters is rejected even when every character is allowed.
  3. If the agent hit this while saving a memory in a conversation, ask it to save the memory again with a simple key, such as project.build-steps. The agent chose that key itself, and a plain key lets the save go through.

What success looks like

  • The memory appears in the Memory Editor's Memories list under the new key (keys are shown in lowercase).

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the key you tried, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep saving with the same key unchanged; it will be rejected every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Memory key validation (normalize_key) rejected the key because it is not a string or does not match ^[a-zA-Z0-9._:-]{1,160}$.

What this means

  • Memory key normalization rejects a non-string or a key outside its 1–160-character ASCII grammar. Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.

Why this can happen

  • Memory key normalization rejects a non-string or a key outside its 1–160-character ASCII grammar.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the key separately from the JSON value and account for case normalization.

How to fix it

  • Supply an ASCII key of 1–160 characters using only letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' or '-' (keys are stored lowercased). The check is normalize_key in src/agent_runtime/skills/memory/models.py; the store is not written when it fails.
  • Use an ASCII key containing letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens within the advertised key limit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The accepted normalized key addresses the intended global Memory entry.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Memory validation and conditional writes preserve the current stored revision on rejection. This is global Memory, separate from conversation KV; diagnostic rendering does not perform additional storage operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
